alternatives.argument: The authored definition fixes C*=Hom_k(C,k), the convolution product (f*g)(c)=(f⊗g)Δ(c), unit ε, and rationality by a finite tensor representing each orbit. Baker §2.3 and UCSD §1.6 independently state this construction; the local theorem proves its algebra axioms.

The local proof defines the transpose comultiplication through the finite tensor-dual isomorphism, verifies its axioms by evaluation on triples and units, checks both map directions, and proves finite biduality by a basis and evaluation. UCSD §1.6 and Baker §2.3 independently support the finite-dimensional dual construction.

The local definition gives ρ:M→M⊗C, the coassociativity/counit equations, compatible maps, and embedded subcomodules. UCSD §3.3 and Chin §2 independently state the right coaction direction and map convention.

The current accepted local proof establishes convolution and the comodule evaluation action in1.1–1.2. Step1.3 proves forward rationality without AC and then proves finite-tensor separation for arbitrary C under AC by taking the finite coefficient span, a finite spanning-list basis, an AC complement in C, and extended coordinate functionals. It proves the finite-dimensional-C separation branch without complements or AC. Step1.4 constructs every finite-C module orbit tensor from a finite dual basis. Unique representing tensors define a linear coaction in2.1 without an additional arbitrary selection;3.1 proves counitality,3.2 proves coassociativity by two separation contractions,3.3 proves both directions on maps, and4.1 records the full choice-free finite-C branch. This uses cor-a-linear-subspace-has-a-complement and the explicit finite-span/basis/dimension clauses, not the removed bundled coefficient-extension supplier. UCSD Theorem3.28 supplies source correspondence context; the stated converse, morphism, and choice boundaries are proved locally, not inferred from an unread supplier or a source citation.

The local proof uses independent coefficients in ρ(m), applies coassociativity after quotienting by their first-factor span, invokes the coefficient-separation and tensor-kernel suppliers, and then applies the counit. Chin §2 independently gives the finite coefficient-space construction.

The local proof lifts the kernel coaction using tensor exactness under AC, constructs image and quotient coactions explicitly, proves the first isomorphism theorem, verifies the regular comodule, and compares basis coefficients in both directions. Chin §2 and UCSD §3.3 provide independent formulations.

The local example checks the group-like coalgebra structure, defines the grading coaction, and recovers a unique finite-support grading by coordinate functionals. UCSD Example 1.15 and Exercise 3.2.21 independently supply the group-like coalgebra and grading decomposition.

The local example defines ρ(v_j)=Σ_i v_i⊗c_ij and checks the two coaction equations using the comatrix identities; the planned batch-1 coalgebra supplier remains an explicit unresolved interface to verify. UCSD Example 1.16 independently gives the comatrix coalgebra formulas.
